chunks: And from him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said:

I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) enter the Ka'bah, then intended to be between the two pillars, but was not able to do so, so he prayed beside it. Then he exited and went until he had left the Masjid.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic structure in Mecca

ai.seo_question: Did the Imam pray inside the Ka'bah or outside it?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the flexibility in the location of prayer (*Salah*) within the Ka'bah, demonstrating that while entering the structure is permissible, it is not obligatory. The Imam’s inability to reach the specific spot between the pillars (*al-Rukn*) and his subsequent prayer nearby underscores the principle that the validity of prayer depends on the intention and direction of the Qibla rather than a rigid requirement to occupy a specific architectural point inside the sanctuary.

en.hubeali: And from hi, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘I saw Abu Abdullahasws entering the Kabah, then intended to be between the two pillars, but was not able upon doing so, so heasws Prayed Salaat besides it. Then heasws exited, so heasws went until he had gone out from the Masjid’.
en.sarwar: 9. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“I saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, enter al-Ka‘bah and he (the Imam) wanted between the two pillars; but could not get there, he (the Imam) then performed Salat (prayer) nearby, then went out and continued walking until he left the Masjid.”
